introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
incertitudes: Section B/C : la consigne imprimee (reponse a deux questions de la Section B OU de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois) n'est pas exprimable par les regles de choix (« parmi 2 sur 3 » par section) ; elle est recopiee en entier dans l'introduction. Chaque question de B et C vaut 17 points imprimes (egalite annoncee par le sujet).

Q13 : points imprimes (i)(a) 2, (b) 2, (c) 5, (ii)(a) 3, (b) 2, (c) 3 = 17, conformes. Sur le scan le tableau de (i)(a) n'est imprime que pour 5k (les autres cases sont remplies a la main par un candidat) : les autres cases sont laissees vides dans l'enonce ; les annotations manuscrites (1/60, 59/16...) sont ignorees (la valeur 59/16 manuscrite ne correspond pas au calcul : E(X) = 37/12, Var(X) = 371/144).
Q13(ii) : « binomial distribution » avec 4 hommes et p = 1/5 ; (c) demande la moyenne et la variance de la loi binomiale (np = 0,8 ; npq = 0,64).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A discrete random variable $X$ has probability mass function, $p$ defined by

$$
p(x)=\begin{cases}k(5+2x),&\text{for }x=0,1,2,3,4,5\\[2pt]0,&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}
$$

where $k$ is a constant.

(a) Copy and complete the distribution table. *[2 marks]*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X=x)$ | $5k$ |  |  |  |  |  |
themes: probability mass function of a discrete variable

questions.enonce_markdown:
Find:

(b) the value of the $k$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probabilities add up to $1$:

$$
5k+7k+9k+11k+13k+15k=60k=1\ \Rightarrow\ k=\frac{1}{60}
$$

**$k=\dfrac{1}{60}$.**
themes: probability mass function of a discrete variable

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the mean and variance of $X$. *[5 marks]*
themes: probability mass function of a discrete variable

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) The probability that a man chosen at random from a village owns a car is $\dfrac15$. Four men are chosen at random from the village. Using the binomial distribution, find the probability that:

(a) none of them owns a car, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of men who own a car among $4$: $X\sim B\left(4,\dfrac15\right)$, with $p=\dfrac15$, $q=1-p=\dfrac45$, $n=4$.

$$
P(X=r)=\binom4r p^r q^{4-r}
$$

$$
P(X=0)=\binom40\left(\frac15\right)^0\left(\frac45\right)^4=\frac{256}{625}
$$

**$P(\text{none owns a car})=\dfrac{256}{625}=0.4096$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) one of them owns a car. *[2 marks]*
(c) Find the mean and variance of the distribution. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $B(n,p)$: mean $=np$ and variance $=npq$.

$$
\text{Mean}=4\times\frac15=\frac45=0.8,\qquad \text{Variance}=4\times\frac15\times\frac45=\frac{16}{25}=0.64
$$

**Mean $=0.8$ and variance $=0.64$.**
